<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">
    <!-- 模板: 内容页 - Anthropic 风格 -->
    
    <defs>
        <!-- 卡片渐变 -->
        <linearGradient id="cardGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="0%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#FFFFFF"/>
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#F8FAFC"/>
        </linearGradient>
    </defs>
    
    <!-- 白色背景 -->
    <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
    
    <!-- 顶部橙色装饰条 -->
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="6" fill="#D97757"/>
    
    <!-- 页面标签 -->
    <text x="60" y="55" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="500" fill="#D97757" letter-spacing="2">
        {{PAGE_LABEL}}
    </text>
    
    <!-- 页面标题（核心观点） -->
    <text x="60" y="100" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">
        {{PAGE_TITLE}}
    </text>
    <text x="60" y="135" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">
        {{PAGE_TITLE_LINE2}}
    </text>
    
    <!-- 三列卡片布局 -->
    <!-- 卡片1 - 绿色（推荐/成功） -->
    <g>
        <rect x="60" y="180" width="360" height="420" fill="url(#cardGradient)" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" rx="12"/>
        <rect x="60" y="180" width="360" height="6" fill="#10B981" rx="3"/>
        
        <!-- 图标背景 -->
        <circle cx="130" cy="250" r="35" fill="#10B981" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
        <!-- 图标占位 -->
        <text x="130" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#10B981">💡</text>
        
        <!-- 卡片标题 -->
        <text x="90" y="320" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_1_TITLE}}</text>
        <text x="90" y="348" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_1_SUBTITLE}}</text>
        
        <!-- 卡片内容 -->
        <text x="90" y="400" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_1_LINE1}}</text>
        <text x="90" y="428" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_1_LINE2}}</text>
        <text x="90" y="470" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_1_NOTE1}}</text>
        <text x="90" y="494" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_1_NOTE2}}</text>
        
        <!-- 标签 -->
        <rect x="90" y="545" width="80" height="28" fill="#10B981" fill-opacity="0.1" rx="14"/>
        <text x="130" y="564" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#10B981">{{CARD_1_TAG}}</text>
    </g>
    
    <!-- 卡片2 - 蓝色（流程/架构） -->
    <g>
        <rect x="460" y="180" width="360" height="420" fill="url(#cardGradient)" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" rx="12"/>
        <rect x="460" y="180" width="360" height="6" fill="#4A90D9" rx="3"/>
        
        <!-- 图标背景 -->
        <circle cx="530" cy="250" r="35" fill="#4A90D9" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
        <!-- 图标占位 -->
        <text x="530" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#4A90D9">⚡</text>
        
        <!-- 卡片标题 -->
        <text x="490" y="320" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_2_TITLE}}</text>
        <text x="490" y="348" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_2_SUBTITLE}}</text>
        
        <!-- 卡片内容 -->
        <text x="490" y="400" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_2_LINE1}}</text>
        <text x="490" y="428" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_2_LINE2}}</text>
        <text x="490" y="470" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_2_NOTE1}}</text>
        <text x="490" y="494" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_2_NOTE2}}</text>
        
        <!-- 标签 -->
        <rect x="490" y="545" width="80" height="28" fill="#4A90D9" fill-opacity="0.1" rx="14"/>
        <text x="530" y="564" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#4A90D9">{{CARD_2_TAG}}</text>
    </g>
    
    <!-- 卡片3 - 橙色（关键洞察） -->
    <g>
        <rect x="860" y="180" width="360" height="420" fill="url(#cardGradient)" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" rx="12"/>
        <rect x="860" y="180" width="360" height="6" fill="#D97757" rx="3"/>
        
        <!-- 图标背景 -->
        <circle cx="930" cy="250" r="35" fill="#D97757" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
        <!-- 图标占位 -->
        <text x="930" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#D97757">⚙️</text>
        
        <!-- 卡片标题 -->
        <text x="890" y="320" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_3_TITLE}}</text>
        <text x="890" y="348" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_3_SUBTITLE}}</text>
        
        <!-- 卡片内容 -->
        <text x="890" y="400" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_3_LINE1}}</text>
        <text x="890" y="428" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_3_LINE2}}</text>
        <text x="890" y="470" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_3_NOTE1}}</text>
        <text x="890" y="494" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_3_NOTE2}}</text>
        
        <!-- 标签 -->
        <rect x="890" y="545" width="80" height="28" fill="#D97757" fill-opacity="0.1" rx="14"/>
        <text x="930" y="564" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#D97757">{{CARD_3_TAG}}</text>
    </g>
    
    <!-- 页码 -->
    <text x="640" y="680" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">
        {{PAGE_NUM}} / {{TOTAL_PAGES}}
    </text>

</svg>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">
    <!-- 模板: 结束页 - Anthropic 风格 -->
    
    <defs>
        <!-- 背景渐变 -->
        <linearGradient id="bgGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#1A1A2E"/>
            <stop offset="50%" style="stop-color:#16213E"/>
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#0F0F1A"/>
        </linearGradient>
        <!-- 橙色渐变 -->
        <linearGradient id="accentGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#D97757"/>
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#E8956F"/>
        </linearGradient>
        <!-- 光晕效果 -->
        <radialGradient id="glowOrange" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="50%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#D97757;stop-opacity:0.2"/>
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#D97757;stop-opacity:0"/>
        </radialGradient>
        <radialGradient id="glowBlue" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="50%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#4A90D9;stop-opacity:0.15"/>
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#4A90D9;stop-opacity:0"/>
        </radialGradient>
    </defs>
    
    <!-- 渐变背景 -->
    <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#bgGradient)"/>
    
    <!-- 网格装饰线 -->
    <g stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.02" stroke-width="1">
        <line x1="0" y1="180" x2="1280" y2="180"/>
        <line x1="0" y1="360" x2="1280" y2="360"/>
        <line x1="0" y1="540" x2="1280" y2="540"/>
        <line x1="320" y1="0" x2="320" y2="720"/>
        <line x1="640" y1="0" x2="640" y2="720"/>
        <line x1="960" y1="0" x2="960" y2="720"/>
    </g>
    
    <!-- 光晕效果 -->
    <ellipse cx="300" cy="200" rx="250" ry="180" fill="url(#glowBlue)"/>
    <ellipse cx="980" cy="500" rx="280" ry="200" fill="url(#glowOrange)"/>
    
    <!-- 神经网络连接装饰 -->
    <g stroke="#4A90D9" stroke-opacity="0.3" stroke-width="1" fill="none">
        <path d="M150,150 Q250,100 350,180"/>
        <path d="M350,180 Q420,250 380,320"/>
        <path d="M950,400 Q1050,350 1100,420"/>
        <path d="M1100,420 Q1150,500 1080,550"/>
    </g>
    
    <!-- 节点装饰 -->
    <g fill="#4A90D9" fill-opacity="0.5">
        <circle cx="150" cy="150" r="5"/>
        <circle cx="350" cy="180" r="7"/>
        <circle cx="380" cy="320" r="4"/>
    </g>
    <g fill="#D97757" fill-opacity="0.6">
        <circle cx="950" cy="400" r="6"/>
        <circle cx="1100" cy="420" r="8"/>
        <circle cx="1080" cy="550" r="5"/>
    </g>
    
    <!-- 感谢语标签 -->
    <text x="640" y="240" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="500" fill="#D97757" letter-spacing="3">
        THANK YOU
    </text>
    
    <!-- 主感谢语 -->
    <text x="640" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="52" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">
        {{THANK_YOU}}
    </text>
    
    <!-- 装饰分隔线 -->
    <rect x="540" y="350" width="200" height="3" fill="url(#accentGradient)" rx="1.5"/>
    
    <!-- 副标语 -->
    <text x="640" y="410" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.7">
        {{TAGLINE}}
    </text>
    
    <!-- 联系信息卡片 -->
    <rect x="440" y="460" width="400" height="120" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.05" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.1" stroke-width="1" rx="12"/>
    
    <text x="640" y="505" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">
        {{CONTACT_NAME}}
    </text>
    <text x="640" y="535" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.7">
        {{CONTACT_EMAIL}}
    </text>
    <text x="640" y="560" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.6">
        {{CONTACT_URL}}
    </text>
    
    <!-- 底部分隔线 -->
    <rect x="60" y="640" width="1160" height="1" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
    
    <!-- 底部信息 -->
    <text x="60" y="680" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">
        {{DATE}}
    </text>
    <text x="1220" y="680" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">
        {{COPYRIGHT}}
    </text>

</svg>

    <text x="60" y="55" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="500" fill="#D97757" letter-spacing="2">PROBLEM</text>

    <text x="60" y="95" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">
        SFT Alone Fails to Teach Slot-Filling and Tool Rejection
    </text>

    <!-- Takeaway box -->
    <rect x="60" y="115" width="1160" height="40" fill="#D97757" fill-opacity="0.08" rx="6"/>
    <text x="80" y="141" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1A1A2E">
        TA-LLMs must decide: ask follow-up questions, make tool calls, or reject inappropriate requests. SFT only teaches what TO do — not what NOT to do.
    </text>

    <!-- Three failure mode cards -->
    <!-- Card 1 -->
    <rect x="60" y="185" width="360" height="390" fill="url(#cardGradient)" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" rx="12" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
    <rect x="60" y="185" width="360" height="6" fill="#EF4444" rx="3"/>

    <circle cx="130" cy="250" r="30" fill="#EF4444" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
    <use data-icon="triangle-exclamation" x="106" y="226" width="48" height="48" fill="#EF4444"/>

    <text x="90" y="310" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">Failure Mode 1</text>
    <text x="90" y="338" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#EF4444">Missing Follow-Up Questions</text>

    <text x="90" y="375" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1E293B">User provides incomplete info</text>
    <text x="90" y="400" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1E293B">(e.g., "Book a flight" with no</text>
    <text x="90" y="425" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1E293B">destination or date specified).</text>
    <text x="90" y="460" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">SFT model skips slot-filling and</text>
    <text x="90" y="482" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">proceeds to hallucinate arguments.</text>

    <rect x="90" y="520" width="120" height="28" fill="#EF4444" fill-opacity="0.1" rx="14"/>
    <text x="150" y="539" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#EF4444">Hallucination</text>

    <!-- Card 2 -->
    <rect x="460" y="185" width="360" height="390" fill="url(#cardGradient)" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" rx="12" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
    <rect x="460" y="185" width="360" height="6" fill="#EF4444" rx="3"/>

    <circle cx="530" cy="250" r="30" fill="#EF4444" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
    <use data-icon="circle-exclamation" x="506" y="226" width="48" height="48" fill="#EF4444"/>

    <text x="490" y="310" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">Failure Mode 2</text>
    <text x="490" y="338" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#EF4444">Hallucinated Tool Invocations</text>

    <text x="490" y="375" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1E293B">Model invokes tools with</text>
    <text x="490" y="400" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1E293B">fabricated or incorrect argument</text>
    <text x="490" y="425" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1E293B">values instead of asking user.</text>
    <text x="490" y="460" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Results in wrong API calls and</text>
    <text x="490" y="482" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">downstream errors in production.</text>

    <rect x="490" y="520" width="140" height="28" fill="#EF4444" fill-opacity="0.1" rx="14"/>
    <text x="560" y="539" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#EF4444">Slot Hallucination</text>

    <!-- Card 3 -->
    <rect x="860" y="185" width="360" height="390" fill="url(#cardGradient)" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" rx="12" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
    <rect x="860" y="185" width="360" height="6" fill="#EF4444" rx="3"/>

    <circle cx="930" cy="250" r="30" fill="#EF4444" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
    <use data-icon="ban" x="906" y="226" width="48" height="48" fill="#EF4444"/>

    <text x="890" y="310" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">Failure Mode 3</text>
    <text x="890" y="338" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#EF4444">Failed Tool Rejection</text>

    <text x="890" y="375" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1E293B">User requests functionality</text>
    <text x="890" y="400" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1E293B">that no available tool supports.</text>
    <text x="890" y="425" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1E293B">Model should reject gracefully.</text>
    <text x="890" y="460" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Instead, SFT model fabricates a</text>
    <text x="890" y="482" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">tool call that doesn't exist.</text>

    <rect x="890" y="520" width="130" height="28" fill="#EF4444" fill-opacity="0.1" rx="14"/>
    <text x="955" y="539" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#EF4444">Out-of-Scope</text>

    <!-- Bottom motivation -->
    <rect x="60" y="600" width="1160" height="50" fill="#4A90D9" fill-opacity="0.06" rx="8"/>
    <text x="640" y="631" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#4A90D9">
        Solution: DiaTool-DPO — use preference optimization to teach models what NOT to do via paired trajectory data
    </text>

    <text x="640" y="690" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">2 / 8</text>
</svg>

arguments.content:
# 01_cover

Welcome to this presentation on DiaTool-DPO, a novel method that enhances tool-augmented LLM dialogue through Direct Preference Optimization. This paper introduces a 5-state MDP formulation and automatic paired trajectory construction to improve how LLMs handle slot-filling and tool call rejection — without any human labeling.

Key points: ① DiaTool-DPO targets dialogue flow control in TA-LLMs ② Uses DPO with automatic preference pair construction ③ Achieves near GPT-4o performance on open-source models
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_problem_motivation

[Transition] Let's start by understanding why this work is needed.

Tool-augmented LLMs face three critical failure modes when trained with SFT alone. First, they fail to ask follow-up questions when user queries are incomplete, skipping necessary slot-filling. Second, they hallucinate tool arguments — fabricating values instead of asking the user. Third, they fail to reject out-of-scope requests, generating phantom tool calls for functionality that doesn't exist. [Pause] The core issue is that SFT only teaches the model what correct behavior looks like, but not what incorrect behavior looks like. DiaTool-DPO addresses this gap through preference optimization.

Key points: ① Three failure modes: missing follow-ups, hallucinated invocations, failed rejections ② SFT teaches what TO do but not what NOT to do ③ Preference optimization can fill this gap
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 03_five_state_mdp

[Transition] To systematically address these failures, the authors model the interaction as a Markov Decision Process.

The MDP has five internal states. State 1 is the initial state where out-of-scope requests are rejected immediately. State 2 represents tool selection without complete slots — this is where slot-filling QA happens, potentially repeating N times. State 3 is reached when all arguments are determined. State 4 is the tool execution wait state, and State 5 is the completion state. [Pause] The three query types map to distinct trajectories through these states: Type 1 goes directly from 1 to 3 when all args are provided, Type 2 loops through State 2 for slot-filling, and Type 3 stays at State 1 for rejection.

Key points: ① 5 states capture the full TA-LLM interaction lifecycle ② State 2 has a self-loop for multi-round slot-filling ③ Three query types define three distinct trajectory patterns
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 04_three_query_types

[Transition] Let's look at these three query types in more detail.

Type 1 queries contain all required arguments — like "Book a flight from LAX to JFK on March 5th, economy class." The trajectory is 1→3→4→5, going straight to execution. Type 2 queries are incomplete — like "Book me a flight" without specifying destination or date. The model needs to ask N rounds of follow-up questions, giving a trajectory of 1→(2×N)→3→4→5. [Pause] Type 3 queries request unavailable functionality — like "Write me a poem" when only travel tools exist. The correct behavior is rejection, staying at State 1. These three patterns are the foundation for constructing preference pairs.

Key points: ① Type 1: complete query, direct execution ② Type 2: incomplete query, slot-filling required ③ Type 3: out-of-scope, must reject
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 05_dataset_construction

[Transition] Now for the key innovation — how DiaTool-DPO automatically constructs its training data.

For each query type, the method pairs a chosen trajectory with a rejected one. For Type 1, the chosen path skips slot-filling while the rejected path unnecessarily asks follow-up questions — teaching the model to prevent redundant slot-filling. For Type 2, it's the reverse: the chosen path does ask follow-ups while the rejected path skips them — preventing slot hallucination. For Type 3, the chosen path rejects the request while the rejected path fabricates a tool call. [Pause] The dataset contains roughly 16,000 pairs at both Easy and Hard difficulty levels, all constructed automatically without human annotation. This is a significant practical advantage.

Key points: ① Chosen vs rejected trajectory pairs for each query type ② Three learning lessons: prevent redundant slot-filling, prevent hallucination, enforce rejection ③ ~16K pairs generated automatically, no human labeling needed
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 06_benchmark_results

[Transition] Let's examine how this approach performs on FunctionChat-Bench.

[Data] The results table tells a clear story. SFT + DiaTool-DPO achieves the best Macro Average across all three model sizes. For Prop.-8B, Macro Avg improves from 0.856 to 0.868. For Prop.-3.1B, from 0.791 to 0.818. And for LLaMA-3-8B, the most dramatic jump — from 0.816 to 0.904. [Pause] Critically, DPO-only without SFT performs very poorly — Macro Avg of just 0.199 for LLaMA-3-8B. This confirms that DPO is a complement to SFT, not a replacement.

Key points: ① SFT + DPO consistently best on Macro Avg ② DPO alone is insufficient — must build on SFT foundation ③ LLaMA-3-8B shows the most dramatic improvement
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 07_llama_performance_gains

[Transition] Let's zoom in on the LLaMA-3-8B results, which show the most impressive gains.

[Data] Slot accuracy jumps from 0.639 to 0.917 — that's a 43.5% improvement. Relevance improves from 0.826 to 0.913, a 10.5% gain. [Pause] To put this in context, GPT-4o achieves 94.8% on information gathering and 91% on tool call rejection. Our LLaMA-3-8B with DiaTool-DPO reaches 91.7% on slot accuracy and 91.3% on relevance — essentially matching GPT-4o performance with a much smaller open-source model. The overall Micro Avg goes from 0.844 to 0.905, and Macro Avg from 0.816 to 0.904.

Key points: ① Slot accuracy: +43.5% (0.639→0.917) ② Relevance: +10.5% (0.826→0.913) ③ Near GPT-4o performance on an 8B parameter open-source model
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 08_takeaways

[Transition] Let me leave you with five key takeaways from this work.

First, the MDP formulation with 5 states and 3 query types provides a principled framework for generating preference pairs. Second, automatic dataset construction eliminates the need for expensive human annotation. Third, DPO complements SFT — you need both. Fourth, the biggest gains are in slot-filling and tool rejection, the exact capabilities SFT struggles with. And fifth, the approach is language-agnostic, generalizing from Korean to English, which opens broad applicability for production systems. [Pause] This work points toward a practical path for deploying GPT-4o-level conversational tool use on smaller, more efficient models.

Key points: ① MDP enables systematic preference pairs ② No human labels needed ③ DPO + SFT > either alone ④ Biggest gains in slot-filling and rejection ⑤ Language-agnostic, production-ready
Duration: 3 minutes

Key points: ① DiaTool-DPO targets dialogue flow control in TA-LLMs ② Uses DPO with automatic preference pair construction ③ Achieves near GPT-4o performance on open-source models
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_problem_motivation

[Transition] Let's start by understanding why this work is needed.

Tool-augmented LLMs face three critical failure modes when trained with SFT alone. First, they fail to ask follow-up questions when user queries are incomplete, skipping necessary slot-filling. Second, they hallucinate tool arguments — fabricating values instead of asking the user. Third, they fail to reject out-of-scope requests, generating phantom tool calls for functionality that doesn't exist. [Pause] The core issue is that SFT only teaches the model what correct behavior looks like, but not what incorrect behavior looks like. DiaTool-DPO addresses this gap through preference optimization.

Key points: ① Three failure modes: missing follow-ups, hallucinated invocations, failed rejections ② SFT teaches what TO do but not what NOT to do ③ Preference optimization can fill this gap
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 03_five_state_mdp

[Transition] To systematically address these failures, the authors model the interaction as a Markov Decision Process.

The MDP has five internal states. State 1 is the initial state where out-of-scope requests are rejected immediately. State 2 represents tool selection without complete slots — this is where slot-filling QA happens, potentially repeating N times. State 3 is reached when all arguments are determined. State 4 is the tool execution wait state, and State 5 is the completion state. [Pause] The three query types map to distinct trajectories through these states: Type 1 goes directly from 1 to 3 when all args are provided, Type 2 loops through State 2 for slot-filling, and Type 3 stays at State 1 for rejection.

Key points: ① 5 states capture the full TA-LLM interaction lifecycle ② State 2 has a self-loop for multi-round slot-filling ③ Three query types define three distinct trajectory patterns
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 04_three_query_types

[Transition] Let's look at these three query types in more detail.

Type 1 queries contain all required arguments — like "Book a flight from LAX to JFK on March 5th, economy class." The trajectory is 1→3→4→5, going straight to execution. Type 2 queries are incomplete — like "Book me a flight" without specifying destination or date. The model needs to ask N rounds of follow-up questions, giving a trajectory of 1→(2×N)→3→4→5. [Pause] Type 3 queries request unavailable functionality — like "Write me a poem" when only travel tools exist. The correct behavior is rejection, staying at State 1. These three patterns are the foundation for constructing preference pairs.

Key points: ① Type 1: complete query, direct execution ② Type 2: incomplete query, slot-filling required ③ Type 3: out-of-scope, must reject
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 05_dataset_construction

[Transition] Now for the key innovation — how DiaTool-DPO automatically constructs its training data.

For each query type, the method pairs a chosen trajectory with a rejected one. For Type 1, the chosen path skips slot-filling while the rejected path unnecessarily asks follow-up questions — teaching the model to prevent redundant slot-filling. For Type 2, it's the reverse: the chosen path does ask follow-ups while the rejected path skips them — preventing slot hallucination. For Type 3, the chosen path rejects the request while the rejected path fabricates a tool call. [Pause] The dataset contains roughly 16,000 pairs at both Easy and Hard difficulty levels, all constructed automatically without human annotation. This is a significant practical advantage.

Key points: ① Chosen vs rejected trajectory pairs for each query type ② Three learning lessons: prevent redundant slot-filling, prevent hallucination, enforce rejection ③ ~16K pairs generated automatically, no human labeling needed
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 06_benchmark_results

[Transition] Let's examine how this approach performs on FunctionChat-Bench.

[Data] The results table tells a clear story. SFT + DiaTool-DPO achieves the best Macro Average across all three model sizes. For Prop.-8B, Macro Avg improves from 0.856 to 0.868. For Prop.-3.1B, from 0.791 to 0.818. And for LLaMA-3-8B, the most dramatic jump — from 0.816 to 0.904. [Pause] Critically, DPO-only without SFT performs very poorly — Macro Avg of just 0.199 for LLaMA-3-8B. This confirms that DPO is a complement to SFT, not a replacement.

Key points: ① SFT + DPO consistently best on Macro Avg ② DPO alone is insufficient — must build on SFT foundation ③ LLaMA-3-8B shows the most dramatic improvement
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 07_llama_performance_gains

[Transition] Let's zoom in on the LLaMA-3-8B results, which show the most impressive gains.

[Data] Slot accuracy jumps from 0.639 to 0.917 — that's a 43.5% improvement. Relevance improves from 0.826 to 0.913, a 10.5% gain. [Pause] To put this in context, GPT-4o achieves 94.8% on information gathering and 91% on tool call rejection. Our LLaMA-3-8B with DiaTool-DPO reaches 91.7% on slot accuracy and 91.3% on relevance — essentially matching GPT-4o performance with a much smaller open-source model. The overall Micro Avg goes from 0.844 to 0.905, and Macro Avg from 0.816 to 0.904.

Key points: ① Slot accuracy: +43.5% (0.639→0.917) ② Relevance: +10.5% (0.826→0.913) ③ Near GPT-4o performance on an 8B parameter open-source model
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 08_takeaways

[Transition] Let me leave you with five key takeaways from this work.

First, the MDP formulation with 5 states and 3 query types provides a principled framework for generating preference pairs. Second, automatic dataset construction eliminates the need for expensive human annotation. Third, DPO complements SFT — you need both. Fourth, the biggest gains are in slot-filling and tool rejection, the exact capabilities SFT struggles with. And fifth, the approach is language-agnostic, generalizing from Korean to English, which opens broad applicability for production systems. [Pause] This work points toward a practical path for deploying GPT-4o-level conversational tool use on smaller, more efficient models.

Key points: ① MDP enables systematic preference pairs ② No human labels needed ③ DPO + SFT > either alone ④ Biggest gains in slot-filling and rejection ⑤ Language-agnostic, production-ready
Duration: 3 minutes
